objective: Make the file-media editor visually consistent with the surrounding release-application form without changing any business behavior.
users: Release applicants entering one or more file-media paths in the artifact-registration step

requirements.statement: The file-media title and add action must use the same compact field hierarchy as surrounding form controls.
acceptance: The title no longer appears as a section heading
The add-path action shares the title row and uses a compact icon-and-text button
requirements.source: User selected option 1 after reviewing the current screenshot on 2026-08-20.
counterexample: The file-media title remains substantially larger than form labels
The add button floats separately at the far right with oversized height

requirements.statement: Every path row must use a stable index-input-delete layout with aligned control heights and consistent spacing.
acceptance: Single and multiple rows align to the same three columns
Index, input and delete control remain vertically centered without layout shift
requirements.source: Visual defect shown in the user screenshot.
counterexample: The row number is visually dominant
The delete button sits above or below the input baseline

requirements.statement: The compact layout must remain usable without page-level horizontal overflow on required mobile and desktop viewports.
acceptance: 375x812, 390x844, 430x932 and desktop widths have no document horizontal overflow
Path input and delete action remain reachable
counterexample: A long path widens the drawer
The delete action is clipped on mobile

requirements.statement: Existing file-media state, validation and payload behavior must remain unchanged.
acceptance: Selecting file media still creates the first row
Add and delete change only the intended row count
Frontend build passes without API type changes
counterexample: The fix changes validation or request payload
Adding or deleting a path no longer works

invariants: File-media behavior and payload remain unchanged
Existing Element Plus and design-token conventions are reused
Control dimensions remain stable across content and viewports
constraints: Modify only the file-media markup in ReleaseApplicationDrawer.vue and its local rules in release-prototype.css
Remain on the existing rokey branch
non_goals: Add file browsing, cards or instructional copy

selected_approach.name: Compact standard form row
selected_approach.reason: It matches the surrounding form hierarchy, fixes the reported imbalance with the smallest change surface and avoids another framed container.

alternatives.name: Grouped bordered panel
alternatives.rejected_because: It adds visual weight and an unnecessary nested container.

alternatives.name: One form item per path
alternatives.rejected_because: It consumes too much vertical space for multi-path entry.

components.name: ReleaseApplicationDrawer
components.responsibility: Expose a compact semantic title/action row and stable path rows while retaining existing bindings and handlers.

components.name: release-prototype.css
components.responsibility: Define field hierarchy, spacing, stable columns and mobile constraints for the file-media editor.

interfaces.name: File-media editor state
interfaces.contract: Markup and CSS changes do not alter draft.fileMedia or ReleaseApplicationWrite.

transitions: reuse existing toggle, add and remove handlers
data_flows.output: Unchanged draft.fileMedia payload with improved presentation

error_handling.behavior: Keep existing warning and submission behavior.
Input shrinks within the stable three-column row and the delete control remains visible.

security: No security or authorization behavior changes
performance: Static local layout rules add no meaningful runtime cost
compatibility: No state, API, database or saved-data changes
operations: No migration, configuration or deployment change

verification_strategy.signal: Title, add action and path rows share a coherent field hierarchy and stable alignment.
verification_strategy.method: Authenticated desktop browser inspection with one and multiple rows.

verification_strategy.signal: Required mobile and desktop viewports show reachable controls and no document horizontal overflow.
verification_strategy.method: Browser screenshots and scrollWidth/clientWidth measurements at 375x812, 390x844, 430x932 and desktop.

verification_strategy.signal: Add/delete behavior and production build remain valid.
verification_strategy.method: Interactive browser checks, npm production build and git diff check.

assumptions.text: The reported issue is visual hierarchy and alignment rather than a requested workflow change.
assumptions.basis: The user identified only local style confusion and selected the standard-form-row option.
assumptions.falsifier: The user requests different content, validation or path-entry interaction.

decisions.decision: Use the compact standard-form-row approach without a framed panel.
decisions.reason: It best matches adjacent controls and minimizes visual weight.

decisions.decision: Keep an icon-and-text add action but reduce its visual emphasis.
decisions.reason: The command remains clear without competing with the primary form actions.

decisions.decision: Retain the circular danger delete icon with stable compact dimensions.
decisions.reason: It is familiar, already implemented and appropriate for a row-level destructive action.
decisions.source: Existing UI convention and selected scope.

risks.risk: Element Plus label styling conflicts with the custom title/action row.
risks.impact: Alignment can vary by density or theme.
risks.mitigation: Use dedicated local class names and verify current themes and viewport widths.

risks.risk: Three columns become cramped on narrow mobile widths.
risks.impact: Input or delete control can clip.
risks.mitigation: Use minmax(0, 1fr), compact fixed side columns and explicit overflow measurements.

approval.evidence: The user selected option 1 and explicitly confirmed the landed design on 2026-08-20.
